items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: No disrespect to him, I just don’t think I could do that.

ctx.x: In a general sense could you say what kind of things that you wouldn’t go for?

It’s not so easy because it’s really case by case. In other words, I could never say I won’t take a smooth jazz gig because that’s not true, I might. If somebody called me and said look I’m going to pay you some good money, we want you to come out with this funky smooth jazz band, and Eric, you could just play the way you play. You know, you can kind of do what Miles did. You can put a rock beat behind you but you just play the way you want to play on top of it. I’d do that in a heartbeat. If somebody said I want…

Kenny G, we really want you to get deep into that style. I’d probably have to say I can’t do that. I don’t think I could. No disrespect to him, I just don’t think I could do that. I think I would be miserable. I mean maybe okay, three or four days and the money is massive, yeah I could go ahead and give it a shot, but that would be a tough one.
